Find the eFixition.a Simulation Instability the Entire Gamut file.

Drag it into the 2D or 3D window.  
After the fire simulation, the panels will immediately collide with each other, causing the costume to move continuously.  
This occurs because the panel is not positioned correctly during arrangement.  
In the 3D window, select Rearrange 3D Arrangement, All.  
In the 3D window, the panels will be remodeled before the simulation.  
In the 2D window, select the front panel.  
In the 3D window, right-click and select Rearrange 2D Position Arrangement.  
Select the 2D arrangement of the front panel in the 3D window.  
In the 3D window, right-click on the panel.  
Left-click to select the positional ball.  
Use the quick arrangement tool to align the panels with the front panel.  
Use the positional ball tool to position the panels inside the panel.  
Repeat the operation on the other side.  
Place the panels behind the front panel.  
In the 2D window, select the right-front panel and the right-front panel panel.  
In the 3D window, use the positional ball tool.  
Place the right-front panel on top of the left-front panel.  
Rotate the view to check the distance between the panels.  
Open the arrangement point.  
In the 2D window, select the front panel.  
In the front window arrangement point, click to lower the panel.  
In the 2D window, select the outer panel.  
In the 3D window, use the positional ball tool to drag the outer panel away from the inner panel.  
Rotate the view to check the distance between the panels.  
In the 2D window, select the outer panel of the lower right panel.  
In the 3D window, use the positional ball tool to drag the panel away from the left panel.  
Rotate the view to check the distance between the panels.  
Activate the simulation.  
Check if the clothing can be stabilized.  
Turn off the simulation.

chunks.content: ## Simulation Instability in Entire Garment: Overview This section explains how to address simulation instability issues in CLO when working with entire garment panels. It covers the root cause of panel collisions during simulation and the step-by-step process to properly arrange panels using 2D and 3D tools to ensure stable garment behavior. ## Identifying and Importing the Simulation Instability Project Open the project file related to simulation instability for the entire garment: - Locate the file named **eFixition.a Simulation Instability the Entire Gamut** in the Prentice Files directory. - Drag the file into either the 2D or 3D window in CLO to load the project. - Upon starting the fabric simulation, observe that garment panels immediately collide, causing continuous unwanted movement of the costume. This instability occurs because the garment panels are not correctly positioned or aligned during the initial arrangement phase. ## Correcting Panel Arrangement Using 3D and 2D Tools To fix panel collisions, follow these steps: ### Rearrange All Panels in 3D - In the 3D window, select **Rearrange 3D Arrangement, All**. - This command remodels and repositions all panels in 3D before simulation, providing a baseline arrangement. ### Align Front Panel Using 2D and 3D Windows - In the 2D window, select the **front panel**. - In the 3D window, right-click and select **Rearrange 2D Position Arrangement** to focus on the front panel’s 2D layout. - Right-click the front panel in 3D, then left-click to select the **positional ball** tool. - Use the positional ball to quickly align adjacent panels with the front panel, ensuring correct positioning inside the panel boundary. ### Position Side and Rear Panels - Repeat the alignment process on the opposite side. - Place the panels behind the front panel to avoid overlap. - In the 2D window, select the **right-front panel**. - Use the positional ball tool in the 3D window to position the right-front panel on top of the left-front panel. - Rotate the 3D view to verify appropriate distance and spacing between panels. ### Adjust Arrangement Points for Panel Clearance - Open the **arrangement point** settings. - In the 2D window, select the front panel and lower it by adjusting its arrangement point. - Select outer panels in the 2D window, then use the positional ball in 3D to drag these panels away from inner panels. - For example, move the outer panel of the lower right panel away from the left panel. - Continuously rotate the 3D view to check distances between panels and ensure no overlaps. ## Finalizing and Testing Simulation Stability - Activate the fabric simulation to test if the garment stabilizes without panels colliding. - Observe garment behavior; if panels no longer collide and the costume remains stable, the rearrangement is successful. - Turn off the simulation once verification is complete. --- This procedure ensures proper panel alignment and spacing, preventing garment instability caused by overlapping or incorrectly positioned panels during simulation in CLO.
